subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in TUI observer or mirror mode that can display activity from other channel sessions, and what security boundary must gate that visibility?
rationale: Current main has the low-level per-session event primitive, but cross-channel or cross-agent visibility changes what a TUI client is authorized to see and may require new config or CLI surface.

options.title: Approve scoped read-only observer
options.body: Implement an operator-read-gated TUI observer limited to explicit agents and sessions, with no outbound mirroring until the visibility model is proven.

options.title: Limit this to same-session live tail
options.body: Keep the broad feature deferred and only land the existing selected-session live update fix from the open PR.

options.title: Defer cross-channel visibility
options.body: Close or pause this direction until a fuller security and product design exists for cross-channel and cross-agent exposure.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped read-only observer
recommendation.body: Implement an operator-read-gated TUI observer limited to explicit agents and sessions, with no outbound mirroring until the visibility model is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the TUI session isolation behavior this feature must preserve and are the best available routing owner for the product/security tradeoff.
